Header: Product Pulse customer session with Lumen Therapeutics
Date: 2026-12-08 16:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Omar (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood Marketing), Leah (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair, Ethan Gomez, Samir Das, Aisha Bello (Lumen)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, welcome, this is Maya from Redwood marketing. Thanks for making time. We're aiming for a 30- to 45-minute chat — just a friendly customer spotlight, nothing heavy, and then Omar will get us started.
[00:15] Omar: Thanks, Maya. Hi Priya, Ethan, Samir, thanks for joining. The idea is to capture your deployment journey, what worked, and a couple of quotes for a short case and a social clip. No pressure.
[00:28] Priya: Yeah, thanks. Happy to do this. We've been meaning to share some of the performance numbers, it's been great.
[00:36] Ethan: Quick note — Aisha from our comms team is here to make sure we don't say anything that needs legal review, so if we need to flag quotes that's fine.
[00:44] Omar: Perfect. Maybe start with 1–2 sentences about Lumen and the feature set you're shipping that uses Redwood?
[00:51] Priya: Sure. Lumen builds personalized clinical decision support models — real time guidance for clinicians in the workflow. We run both long-form note summarization and short inline suggestions. The latency constraints are tight for inline — we needed under, like, 200ms end-to-end for the UX to feel instant.
[01:12] Samir: To add, our baseline before Redwood was a mix of self-hosted endpoints and a big batch job. We had spikes and some unpredictable tail latency, and the ops bill was getting scary.
[01:25] Leah: When did you first evaluate Redwood and what was the tipping point?
[01:29] Priya: We piloted Redwood Hosted first, but the turning point was the Dedicated offering — predictable throughput and isolation. The enterprise concerns — audit logs, KMS — pushed us to the Private control plane later.
[01:42] Ethan: Also the observability in the console answered a lot of our questions. Having token-level cost and latency traces let product and finance speak the same language.
[01:55] Omar: Nice. Can you share the headline metrics — latency, cost delta, model footprint? Approx numbers are fine.
[02:02] Priya: Yeah. After moving core low-latency routes to Redwood Dedicated with smart batching and KV cache, our median inference latency dropped from ~120ms to ~45ms at the same QPS. For bursts we saw P95 go from ~500ms to ~120ms.
[02:22] Samir: Cost per 1M tokens dropped roughly 40% once we tuned batching and turned on prefix caching — that came directly from the Optimize recommendations.
[02:33] Ethan: And throughput — we went from a single-host bottleneck to a pool that sustained 3x concurrent sessions without tailing out.
[02:42] Maya: That is a great soundbite — "3x concurrent sessions and 40% lower unit cost" — would you be comfortable if we quote that?
[02:48] Priya: Yeah, that's fine, subject to comms sign-off — Aisha will confirm.
[02:52] Aisha: Yup we'll confirm the exact phrasing.
[02:58] Omar: On the technical side, Leah, can you summarize what the SE work looked like during onboarding?
[03:04] Leah: Sure — we did an initial throughput characterization, suggested model quantization profiles, and enabled continuous batching with a short tail latency cap. We also set up the KV prefix cache for long-form note context which cut repeated token compute. There was a small tweak around tokenization differences that Samir had to align with their tokenizer mapping.
[03:26] Samir: Right — there was one gotcha. The tokenizer splitting on special characters caused different token counts between our preprocessor and the model checkpoint. Leah's team helped map the tokenizer and update the preproc stage, which reduced unexpected cost spikes.
[03:40] Leah: Also we recommended using a dedicated GPU pool with an autoscale policy and a warm standby to handle the nighttime batch jobs without degrading the inline latency.
[03:50] Priya: The warm standby trick was super helpful — otherwise we'd get cold starts that annoyed clinicians.
[03:55] Omar: Switching gears to security and compliance — you mentioned Private earlier. Can you walk us through why Private mattered and what the process was like?
[04:03] Priya: For us, patient data residency and auditability are non-negotiable. Redwood Private let us keep the control plane in our VPC, integrate with our KMS, and retain audit logs for 7 years — which matches our internal policy. The deployment checklist was heavy but straightforward; Leah helped with the Terraform bits.
[04:24] Ethan: From legal side the SOC2 docs and the ISO references the Redwood team provided accelerated review. The SSO and RBAC integration saved weeks of back-and-forth.
[04:33] Aisha: The only hiccup was an initial question around data retention default policies — we asked for a custom retention window and Redwood accommodated that in the setup.
[04:45] Maya: Great note for others in regulated spaces. For the case write-up, do you have any preferred quotes or messaging you want highlighted?
[04:52] Priya: Emphasize reliability and clinician experience — something like: "Redwood made our inference predictable at scale, which let us ship a confident clinician-facing feature." But again, Aisha will finalize the wording.
[05:05] Ethan: Also the cost number is compelling, product folks love that.
[05:10] Omar: Wonderful. Quick question on benchmarks — Leah, you were going to share a spreadsheet with the runs, right?
[05:16] Leah: Yep, I'll drop the benchmark spreadsheet to the shared drive after this call and link it in the follow-up. It'll have the before/after configs, instance types, batch window, and tokenization notes.
[05:26] Samir: One small note — we ran a custom reranking route for triage that used a lighter model on Redwood and a heavier re-ranker in-house. The routing policies were useful — we set fallback to a cheaper model during high load and it kept the UX consistent.
[05:43] Omar: Nice example of graceful degradation. Any comments on support experience?
[05:48] Priya: Support was responsive. We had a high-severity incident during a config rollout and the SE team was on the call; the postmortem and a mitigation patch were delivered within 48 hours which was impressive.
[06:01] Aisha: From a comms perspective that's good to record as it shows operational readiness.
[06:07] Maya: We'll likely ask for a short video clip — 30s to 45s — with a quote. Is someone comfortable being on camera?
[06:13] Priya: I can do a 30-second quote. Ethan might do a short b-roll with the product.
[06:18] Aisha: We'll coordinate availability — week of the 21st looks best.
[06:24] Omar: For legal, we'll route the draft copy and the quote release through Aisha. Anything else we should cover?
[06:30] Ethan: Maybe one thing — what's the recommended short blurb for devs about the technical integration steps? Something a new team can replicate quickly.
[06:38] Leah: Short blurb: 1) map tokenizer and preproc; 2) run throughput char to pick batch window; 3) enable prefix KV caching for repeated contexts; 4) set up dedicated pool with warm standby; 5) plug-in KMS and audit logs for Private. We'll give a one-pager.
[06:58] Samir: That one-pager will be gold for our internal onboarding too.
[07:03] Maya: Perfect, we'll include that as an asset. Any competitors or alternative approaches you considered before choosing Redwood?
[07:10] Priya: We considered a handful: vendor-managed endpoints from major cloud providers, a Triton + custom infra path, and a couple of fully-managed LLM API vendors. The deciding factor was the unified runtime + observability and the ability to move between hosted/dedicated/private without re-architecting.
[07:29] Omar: Last section — marketing logistics. We'll create a short Q&A doc and a one-paragraph case. Then we'll ask you to approve the quote. Maya will coordinate the recording.
[07:39] Maya: Thanks. We'll also include a short form for quote permissions, nothing legal heavy.
[07:45] Aisha: Sounds good, send to my email and we'll route it.
[07:49] Omar: Great. We'll follow up with the draft and the benchmark link. Leah will add the technical runbook.
[07:55] Priya: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the partnership.
[08:00] Maya: Thank you — end of recording.
---
Notes on transcript: some words auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Triton" rendered as "Tried on" in one segment). There were short overlaps towards the end when coordinating scheduling.
